reviewNote: Drafted by Claude for faculty review from the Carson-Newman scenario. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Outpatient lap chole in a young woman with mild intermittent asthma, latex allergy, codeine intolerance, OCP use, and severe prior PONV with motion sickness (Apfel 4). The CN teaching case: characterize asthma control, plan multimodal PONV prophylaxis, examine the airway, avoid codeine.

asa.rationale: Mild intermittent asthma is mild systemic disease.

decision.rationale: Asthma is well controlled; the risks are planned for, not reasons to delay.

redFlags.evidence: Female, non smoker, severe PONV after 2012 sedation, motion sickness, postop opioids.
redFlags.implication: Very likely PONV and delayed discharge.
redFlags.action: Multimodal prophylaxis: dexamethasone, ondansetron, scopolamine patch or TIVA, minimize opioids.

redFlags.implication: Bronchospasm at intubation or with light anesthesia.
redFlags.action: Confirm control, albuterol before induction, deep plane before airway, sevoflurane, albuterol ready.

redFlags.implication: Reaction risk from gloves, catheters, equipment.
redFlags.action: Latex free room and supplies, first case of the day when possible.

redFlags.finding: Codeine listed as allergy but is an intolerance (nausea)
redFlags.implication: Codeine worsens nausea; not a true allergy.
redFlags.action: Clarify, avoid codeine, multimodal non opioid analgesia.

redFlags.implication: Plan cannot rely on an undocumented exam.
redFlags.action: Examine and document the airway before induction (it is reassuring: Mallampati I).

planItems.item: Multimodal PONV prophylaxis (two or more agents)
ETT with a deep plane before instrumentation; albuterol ready

cnRubric.title: Carson-Newman teaching case: Lap chole, reactive airway, PONV
